summary: Ozark County lookout site where a new tower was erected in 1952-53; a 1953 survey describes a four-legged steel tower, and the Missouri Department of Conservation's area page says its towers serve radio relay and wildfire detection.

facts.design: Four-legged steel tower, painted aluminum (1953 survey description); the 2015 plan calls the current tower self-supported and does not give its material

access.note: The conservation area is open to the public daily from 4 a.m. to 10 p.m. The tower is a working fire-detection and radio structure, and the access road is closed to vehicles when the tower is not manned.

events.note: Towersite acquired in fiscal 1951-52, per the Missouri Conservation Commission annual report
New tower erected in fiscal 1952-53; a 1953 survey description already describes the steel tower
Area plan describes a new self-supported tower carrying radio relays and used by department staff for fire detection

notes_for_editor: The 2015 plan calls the Timber Knob tower new but does not date it, and no source says whether the 1953 tower still stands or was replaced. Current status rests on the department's area page and the 2015 plan, not a site visit. The 2015 plan has a line 'Area is not open to the public' in a section I could not tie to Timber Knob (the area page says it is open daily); it was not used. Height 15.2 m comes from the 1953 survey's 'about 50 feet' and may not match the current tower. Access is rated restricted for climbing: the area is public, but the tower is a working fire-detection structure and no source describes public climbing. Name correction proposed: Timbered Knob to Timber Knob. Fact check 2026-10-21: the story now calls the site a fire lookout site and attributes the steel construction to the 1953 survey only, because no source gives the current tower's material. The unsourced climbing advice was removed from the story.
